confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly describes "two randomized writing task blocks (treatment and control)". Figure 1 places a randomization bracket and die beneath the two blocks, supporting randomized within-person condition order.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, section 4 opening paragraph and Figure 1 (text extracted and figure visually checked).

confirmed.statement: S1 also randomizes task allocation: each of the 81 analyzed participants chose six tasks, with four randomly selected for treatment and two for control. Both conditions therefore involve the same participants.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, section 4, Writing Task and Task-Level Survey; p. 24, Table 9 caption.

confirmed.statement: S1 treatment supplies an LLM-generated initial draft based on the participant's planned content, which the participant edits to express personal style. AI-generated material assists production of the participant's own final text; this is not merely evaluation of differently attributed outputs.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Figure 2 and section 4; p. 5, continuation of section 4; p. 24, Appendix D consent and tutorial instructions.

confirmed.statement: The S1 draft generator is named GPT-o4-mini. It generates prose from the writing-task prompt and participant-written details, supporting the generative_ai classification and the described initial-draft/post-editing role.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 5.1, Generation of LLM Drafts, and Prompt 4.1.

confirmed.statement: S1 control participants write directly from their own plans without seeing any LLM-generated text for those tasks, matching the form's no-AI comparator.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, continuation of section 4: "In the control block, participants wrote at least 150 characters directly from their plans without seeing any LLM-generated text."

confirmed.statement: Original unedited LLM drafts are an intermediate stage of S1 treatment, followed by the participant's post-edits; they are not an independently assigned participant arm.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Figure 2; p. 5, section 4 treatment procedure and section 6.1 before/after analysis.

confirmed.statement: S1 reports 100 recruited and 81 retained after excluding incomplete sessions and participants who never edited any LLM draft. Table 9 confirms that all 81 contribute treatment and control tasks, matching the analyzed counts in both arms.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Appendix A.1; p. 24, Table 9 caption.

confirmed.statement: The paper describes S1 as preregistered and gives a preregistration link, supporting assignment.preregistered. This verification uses the saved paper; the linked preregistration was not needed to establish the reported assignment.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, Introduction and footnote 2; p. 3, section 3 and footnote 5.

confirmed.statement: S2 explicitly randomizes presentation of candidate writing scenarios. Respondents select scenarios where personal style matters; they are not assigned AI assistance or asked to produce scored writing, consistent with the form's stated restriction on this randomization.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 22, Appendix C opening paragraph; p. 23, Appendix C survey instructions and results.

confirmed.statement: S2 reports 102 survey completers and 88 passing attention checks, matching the form's analyzed arm count. Its participants could not also complete the main study, so S2 does not supply additional AI-assistance assignment evidence for S1.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 23, Appendix C, paragraph beginning "102 participants completed this formative survey".

summary: S1 supports randomized condition order and task allocation for GPT-o4-mini post-editing versus unassisted writing. S2 only randomizes scenario presentation, as coded, so no assignment-coding error was found and criterion 1 holds through S1.
